name: iota-frame-signature
authority: The received {e, i, iota} interpretation frame and the received pure-iota process package, both already in this repository at pinned digests, together with the four-frame layout retained by note 0224. This contract authorizes one bounded exact computation over declared finite rational matrices and nothing else. It does not authorize a physical interpretation, a new native operation, a stable type, a transport, or a changed frame profile.
question: Under the received frame's own transport obligation, which metric signatures can a carrier carry while the declared complex structure J (J squared = -I) stays compatible with the metric, meaning J-transpose G J = G? Is any signature with exactly one negative direction reachable on a four-dimensional carrier, and if not, what exactly does a Lorentzian signature cost: which frame obligation is given up, and is that signature reachable at all under some other declared structure on the same carrier?
level: External exact finite rational linear algebra: exact solution of a linear system over Q, exact congruence reduction for the inertia of a symmetric rational form, and exhaustive enumeration of a declared finite family of integer matrices with a declared entry range. Every acceptance test compares integers or exact rationals; no floating-point value enters any of them, and no eigenvalue is approximated. Standard library only.
sources: The complex structure J, the cut operator convention H0 = L/(2 d_max) with denominator one for the empty-edge case, H = diag(H0,H0), the initial metric G = I and the initial observer O = I, and the chart transport rule that keeps H, J, G and O together, are quoted from knowledge/received/iota-frame-knowledge-2026-09-17-v1/materials/frame.md at SHA-256 d8967cc3e6b953d547a22010f37d9997a023d1b55935928f88becba86862dae0.

The received process chain-and-single, with its declared source, events, cut masks and cut-graph edges, is read from knowledge/received/iota-process-knowledge-2026-09-17-v1/materials/interpretations.json at SHA-256 8009db7b8828ae76aa01b25684b9aa974fc91c4fcb64a439946701a49fe528b1, and is used only to build the frame's own twelve-dimensional instance.
The retained layout of note 0224 supplies the four towers' carriers and their dimensions; it is not recomputed here and is cited as a bounded external experiment of this repository.
The pinned digests are cross-checked against the receiver's own record of its previous materials, so a pin that agrees only with this contract and not with the received record fails the run.
domain: The complex structure J = [[0, -I], [I, 0]] on Q to the 2n for n = 1, 2, 3 and 6; the linear system J-transpose G J = G in all 4 n squared entries of G, with and without the symmetry of G; the inertia of a symmetric rational form by exact congruence reduction; a declared finite family of integer matrices in a declared entry range for n = 1, 2, 3; the frame's own twelve-dimensional instance built from the received process chain-and-single; and one declared four-dimensional instance with one declared Lorentzian metric and one declared involutive structure.

minimal_four_dimensional_instance.comment: two cuts joined by one edge: the cut graph of a one-event process, so d_max is one and the frame's denominator is two

exhaustive_families.comment: symmetric J-compatible matrices are parametrised by A symmetric with n(n+1)/2 free entries and B antisymmetric with n(n-1)/2 free entries, so n squared in all; the declared range makes each family finite and the inertia of every nondegenerate member is computed

refusals: reading a compatible signature as a physical spacetime, a light cone, a causal order or a clock
reading the frame's continuous operator parameter as a time coordinate
claiming that a Lorentzian signature is unreachable in general, when the computation shows it is unreachable only while the complex structure stays metric-compatible
claiming that the four towers of note 0224 have four-dimensional carriers, or that any of their carriers is Lorentzian
treating a characteristic polynomial, a determinant or a trace as a signature without computing the inertia
reading an exact inertia computation on declared rational matrices as a statement about a manifold

quantifiers: every entry of the linear system J-transpose G J = G, solved exactly, for n = 1, 2 and 3
every solution of that system, checked for commutation with J, on a complete basis of the solution space
every symmetric nondegenerate member of each declared finite integer family, for its inertia
every pair of even inertia indices summing to four, for the exhaustive four-dimensional conclusion
every entry of the two declared four-dimensional residual matrices
every declared structural identity of the involution, the Lorentzian metric and the complex structures
grammar: exact rational Gaussian elimination for the solution space of a linear system
exact rational symmetric congruence reduction for the inertia, with one-by-one and two-by-two pivots and no eigenvalue approximation
matrix arithmetic over Fractions with the complex structure built from blocks
declared integer parametrisations enumerated exhaustively in a declared range
acceptance: The frame's own twelve-dimensional instance is rebuilt from the received process and satisfies J squared = -I, H symmetric, H J = J H and A = -J H skew, with H0 = L/6 and degrees two, three, two, two, three, two; its metric G = I is J-compatible and its inertia is twelve positive and zero negative.

For n equal to one, two and three the solution space of J-transpose G J = G has dimension 2 n squared, and the symmetric solutions form a subspace of dimension n squared, with a basis whose every member commutes with J.

Every symmetric nondegenerate member of every declared finite family has both inertia indices even, exhaustively over the declared range, and the counts of examined, degenerate and nondegenerate members are reported.

On a four-dimensional carrier the only signatures with both indices even are four zero, two two and zero four; the signatures three one and one three do not occur, so exactly one negative direction is unreachable while the complex structure stays metric-compatible.

On the declared four-dimensional instance the frame's own metric G = I makes A = -J H skew exactly, while the declared Lorentzian metric G = diag(1,1,1,-1) does not: both the residual J-transpose G J - G and the residual A-transpose G + G A are recorded exactly and are not zero, so the frame identity that the run checks under G = I fails at first order under that metric.

The declared involution K = diag(1,1,-1,-1) satisfies K squared = the identity and K-transpose G K = G for the same Lorentzian G, while K is neither J nor minus J and K squared is not minus the identity; hence a signature with exactly one negative direction is reachable on a four-dimensional carrier exactly when the structure is an involution rather than a complex structure.
No acceptance test compares a floating-point value, no eigenvalue is approximated, and the checker imports nothing outside the standard library.
protected: No physical claim is made anywhere in this experiment. A signature is a property of a declared rational symmetric form on a declared finite carrier. Nothing here asserts a spacetime, a manifold, a light cone, a causal order, a curvature, a mass, a physical clock or a simultaneity, and no physical interpretation of the frame is created.

The result is a statement about metric compatibility, not about reachability in general: a Lorentzian signature is shown unreachable while the complex structure stays metric-compatible, and is shown reachable under a declared involution. The frame's own exponential and Wick coefficient identity is not re-derived under that involution, and what it would become is not decided here.

The four towers of note 0224 are cited, not recomputed. Their carriers have dimension two, twelve, twenty-two and thirty-two, so none of them is a four-dimensional carrier and none of them is the object the Lorentzian question is asked about.

An exact inertia on declared rational matrices is not a theorem about all real forms, and the exhaustive families are finite and declared: their ranges are part of the claim, and a different range is a different run.
The received materials are read-only. Nothing under knowledge/, spec/ or the library catalogue is modified, and no new transport, receipt, exchange or acknowledgment is executed or claimed.

No stable API change: no ValueType, no OperationSpec, no IR version, no Lisp builtin, no parser, type-checker, evaluator or lineage-table change, no Seal, no claim promotion beyond bounded-external-experiment.
Native admission is NotGranted, native execution is NotRun and new transport is NotRun. The functions named inertia and solve in this file are finite exact computations, not Adva operations.
No floating-point value enters any acceptance test, and the run installs no address-space ceiling because it launches no child process, so the repository's portability inventory is unaffected.

A corrected statement is recorded rather than a silently repaired one: the four-frame note 0224 left the signature question open, and this run decides it; the earlier reading that a split structure must give two positives and two negatives on a four-dimensional carrier is wrong and is recorded as wrong in the note that reports this run.
residual: What is established is a set of exact statements about declared finite rational matrices. The solutions of the frame's compatibility condition J-transpose G J = G form a space of dimension 2 n squared, the symmetric solutions among them a space of dimension n squared, and every solution commutes with J; over declared finite integer families every symmetric nondegenerate solution has both inertia indices even; on a four-dimensional carrier that leaves exactly the signatures four zero, two two and zero four, so exactly one negative direction is unreachable while J stays metric-compatible; the frame's own metric G = I makes the generator A = -J H skew exactly, and the declared Lorentzian metric does not, with both exact residuals retained; and a signature with exactly one negative direction is reachable on the same carrier once the structure is the declared involution K with K squared equal to the identity, for which K-transpose G K = G holds. What is not established: whether a K-compatible carrier keeps any of the frame's other obligations, what the frame's exponential and Wick coefficient identity becomes under K, whether a carrier with a Lorentzian signature and any structure can be given a causal order, an observer, a clock or a dynamics, whether the frame's carriers can be given a manifold structure at all, and anything about physical spacetime. Also not established: whether the complex structure could be kept while the metric compatibility is weakened by a declared factor rather than abandoned, which is a different question and is not asked here. The retained correction is part of this run's result: the earlier expectation that an involutive structure must give two positives and two negatives on a four-dimensional carrier is false, and the arithmetical reason is that a metric compatible with an involution is only required to be block diagonal in the involution's eigenspaces, whose two ranks need not be equal. No computation outside a contract counts as a result of this repository.
